I found four defects in the change, all reproduced on both base and head, plus two minor observations. I reviewed branch `refactor/router-tree` at head `1e70f7c` against merge-base `016ab76` (`main`). The working tree was clean, so I reviewed committed changes only.

**How I ran the comparison:** both revisions ran in the provided venv (Starlette 1.2.1), and each log prints which `fastapi` it loaded. A full worktree for the base failed with "no space left on device", so I extracted only the base's `fastapi/` package with `git archive`. Your checkout is untouched apart from the ignored `.scratch/` folder. The existing test suite passes at head (3181 passed, 13 skipped, 5 xfailed), so none of the four below is caught by current tests.

To reproduce, from `.scratch/router-tree/`:
`PYTHONPATH=<checkout> <venv>/bin/python probes.py` (or `probes2.py`)

## Defects

1. **`scope["route"]` for a route in an included router no longer carries the prefix or the include-level settings.**
   - **Where:** `fastapi/routing.py:1593` (`scope["route"] = original_route`) and `fastapi/routing.py:1162`.
   - **Trigger:** `app.include_router(router, prefix="/api", dependencies=[...])`, then any middleware, dependency or endpoint that reads `request.scope["route"]`.
   - **Result:**
     - Base gives `path='/api/items/{item_id}'` and 1 dependency.
     - Head gives `path='/items/{item_id}'` and 0 dependencies, in both the endpoint and the middleware.
     - Included WebSocket routes still report `/api/ws`, so HTTP and WebSocket now disagree.
   - **Why it matters:** `tests/test_route_scope.py` treats `scope["route"].path` as the route's full path. Metrics, logging and tracing code that labels requests by route template will lose the prefix and merge different routes under one label. The release notes list `router.routes` as a breaking change, but they don't mention `scope["route"]`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (P1 in `probes.py`, logs `base.log` / `head.log`).

2. **A bad `include_router` configuration now fails on every request instead of at startup.**
   - **Where:** `fastapi/routing.py:2450–2461` (inclusion now only records the settings) and `_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates`, where routes are built on first use.
   - **Trigger:** `app.include_router(router, prefix="/r", responses={204: {"model": M}})`.
   - **Result:**
     - Base raises `AssertionError: Status code 204 must not have a response body` during `include_router`.
     - Head accepts the include. Then every `GET /r/ok` returns 500, while other routes (`/root`) keep returning 200.
   - **Why it matters:** an app with a configuration mistake now starts and passes health checks on unaffected routes, and the error only shows up in production requests. Any check that `_populate_api_route_state` makes on the combined settings behaves the same way.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (P3).

3. **Callbacks from a callback router that includes another router are dropped from OpenAPI.**
   - **Where:** `fastapi/openapi/utils.py:325–326`. The loop keeps only `isinstance(callback, routing.APIRoute)` entries, so the new included-router objects are skipped. Model collection (`get_fields_from_routes`) does handle them, so the two parts are now inconsistent.
   - **Trigger:** `cb_router.include_router(cb_inner)`, then `@app.post(..., callbacks=cb_router.routes)`.
   - **Result:** base outputs the `event` callback operation; head outputs `"callbacks": {}`.
   - **Why it matters:** generated clients and docs silently lose the callback definitions.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (P4).

4. **A schema assigned to `app.openapi_schema` is now discarded and regenerated.**
   - **Where:** `fastapi/applications.py:1083–1084`. `_openapi_routes_version` starts as `None`, so the first `openapi()` call always regenerates.
   - **Trigger:** set `app.openapi_schema = {...}` without overriding `app.openapi`, then request `/openapi.json`.
   - **Result:** base serves the assigned schema (`title: custom`); head serves a generated one (`title: FastAPI`).
   - **Why it matters:** apps that serve a fixed, pre-built schema this way silently serve a different one. The documented pattern that overrides `app.openapi` with a custom function is unaffected.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (P5). **Action:** you decide — whether assigning `openapi_schema` directly is a supported pattern is the open question below.

## Minor observations

- **Mounts added to an included router after the first request are never routed.** The new "add after include" behaviour works for path operations: a route added after a request answers 200. A `sub.mount(...)` added after a request stays 404, because `Router.mount` doesn't trigger a rebuild of the included router's cached routes (only `add_route`, `add_websocket_route`, `add_api_route`, `add_api_websocket_route` and `include_router` do). It returns 200 if no request has happened yet. Base never supported adding anything after include, so this is an incomplete feature rather than a regression. Executed (`probes2.py`).
- **Extra work on every request (inferred, not timed).** For each included router, every match walks that router's whole subtree to check whether routes changed (`_get_routes_version`). Every included-route request also rebuilds its handler (`request_response(self.get_route_handler())`). How much this costs depends on how many routes and how much nesting an app has. The docs now say inclusion avoids per-request overhead, which this contradicts. To settle it, benchmark requests per second on base and head with a few hundred nested routes.

## Questions for the author

- Is assigning `app.openapi_schema` directly (without overriding `app.openapi`) meant to keep working? That decides whether item 4 needs a fix or a release note.
- Should `scope["route"]` for an included HTTP route show the full effective route (prefix and combined dependencies), as it did before and still does for WebSockets? If not, item 1 at least needs a release note.

## Checked, no defect found

- Including the same router twice under two prefixes: routing and OpenAPI paths are correct, and `url_for` behaves the same as on base.
- An app-level `generate_unique_id_function` that reads `tags[0]`: raises at decoration time on both base and head.
- Inherited settings when routers are nested (dependencies, tags, responses, deprecated, `include_in_schema`, response class, `strict_content_type`, unique-ID function): I traced the lookup order by reading the code, and it matches base.

Not covered: the translated docs, and third-party consumers of `app.routes`, which the release notes already list as a breaking change.

Probe scripts, logs and notes are in `.scratch/router-tree/` (`NOTES.md` has the dropped leads).

## Scope

- **Head:** `refactor/router-tree` @ `1e70f7c`. **Base:** merge-base with `main` @ `016ab76`. The working tree was clean, so only committed changes are reviewed.
- **Read:** the whole diff of `fastapi/routing.py`, `fastapi/applications.py`, `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`, the docs and `docs_src` changes, the release notes, and the test changes.
- **Probes:** the venv you named, with `PYTHONPATH` set to a `git archive` export of `fastapi/` at each revision. A full `git worktree` couldn't be created because `/tmp` is out of inodes (100% used). Scripts and outputs are in `.scratch/router-tree/` (`probe1.py`, `probe2.py`, `probe3.py`, and matching `.out` files).
- **Test suite at head:** all tests pass (3181 passed, 13 skipped, 5 xfailed).

## Defects

1. **`request.scope["route"]` now points to the un-prefixed route object for included HTTP routes.** At `fastapi/routing.py:1162` and `:1593`, the original `APIRoute` is placed in the scope instead of a route that carries the include-time settings.
   - **Trigger:** `app.include_router(router, prefix="/items", tags=[...], dependencies=[...])`, then reading `request.scope["route"]` from an endpoint or middleware.
   - **Consequence:**
     - `.path` and `.path_format` lose the include prefix: `/{item_id}` instead of `/items/{item_id}`.
     - `.tags` and `.dependencies` lose the include-level values: `{'tags': [], 'deps': 0}` instead of `{'tags': ['T'], 'deps': 1}`.
     - Tools that name metrics or traces after the route template will merge `/items/{id}` and `/users/{id}` into `/{id}`.
     - It is inconsistent: included **websocket** routes still report `/ws/{i}`.
     - `tests/test_route_scope.py` pins `scope["route"].path` as the full template for routes added directly to the app. The release notes' breaking-change list covers `router.routes` but not `scope["route"]`.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`probe1.py` case A, `probe2.py` cases I and R).
     - base: `{'path': '/items/{item_id}', ...}`
     - head: `{'path': '/{item_id}', ...}`
   - **Action:** you decide. Either put the effective route context (or a route-like view of it) in the scope, or list this as a breaking change.

2. **`FastAPI.openapi()` replaces an `app.openapi_schema` that was set directly** (`fastapi/applications.py:1083-1084`). `_openapi_routes_version` starts as `None`, so the version comparison is always unequal the first time, and the schema is regenerated.
   - **Trigger:** assigning `app.openapi_schema = {...}` (for example, a static or pre-built schema) without overriding `app.openapi`.
   - **Consequence:** both `app.openapi()` and `/openapi.json` serve the generated schema instead of the assigned one. Nothing signals the change.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`probe1.py` case B).
     - base: `{'title': 'custom', 'version': '9'}`
     - head: `{'title': 'FastAPI', 'version': '0.1.0'}`
   - The documented `custom_openapi` override pattern replaces `app.openapi` entirely, so it is not affected.

3. **The "prefix and path both empty" check now rejects valid nested includes** (`fastapi/routing.py:2438`). For a nested `_IncludedRouter`, `_iter_included_route_candidates` yields the original `APIRoute`, whose path is relative to its own include. The prefix that the inner include added is not part of it.
   - **Trigger:**
     1. `inner.get("")`
     2. `mid.include_router(inner, prefix="/b")`
     3. `app.include_router(mid)` with no prefix
   - **Consequence:** `FastAPIError: Prefix and path cannot be both empty (path operation: root)` is raised at startup. Base serves `/b`.
   - **Origin:** new.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`probe1.py` case C). Base: `ok`. Head: the exception above.

4. **The cache of included candidates goes stale after the first request** (`_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates`, `fastapi/routing.py:1431`). Only `add_route`, `add_websocket_route`, `add_api_route`, `add_api_websocket_route` and `include_router` increment `_routes_version`. Starlette's `Router.mount()` and `Router.host()` append to `self.routes` without incrementing it, and `APIRouter` inherits both.
   - **Trigger:** `router.mount(...)` on a router that is already included, after a request has been served.
   - **Consequence:** the new mount returns 404. The same call made before the first request returns 200. The release note says "adding routes after a router is included now works", so the result depends on timing.
   - **Origin:** new. Base never served mounts from included routers.
   - **Evidence:** executed (`probe3.py`).
     - head: `mount before first request -> 200`, `mount after first request -> 404`
     - base: 404 in both cases
   - **Fix:** override `mount` and `host` to call `_mark_routes_changed()`.

## Minor observations

- **The route handler is rebuilt on every request to an included route.** `APIRoute.handle` (`fastapi/routing.py:1180`) calls `request_response(self.get_route_handler())` per request. A custom `get_route_handler` ran 5 times over 5 requests on head and 0 times on base. 1000-request timings showed no measurable difference for a trivial endpoint (`probe1.py` case H). It matters only for custom route classes that do expensive or side-effecting work in `get_route_handler`. The new docs say inclusion avoids "adding overhead to each request".

## Outside the change

- **The streaming item schema is lost for routes in included routers.** An endpoint returning `AsyncIterable[Item]`, included through `include_router`, gets `"itemSchema": {}`. The same endpoint on the app directly gets `{"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Item"}`. Base and head behave identically (`probe2.py` case Q, `probe3.py`).
  - **Cause:** `from_api_route` (and the old cloning code) passes the already-resolved `response_model=None`, so `stream_item_type` is never derived again.
  - **Origin:** pre-existing; the refactor kept it.

## Questions for the author

- Is `request.scope["route"]` meant to stay the user's original `APIRoute` (identity preserved for custom subclasses), or should it carry the effective path, tags and dependencies? Either way, defect 1 needs a decision or a release-note entry.

## Checked with no defect found

These behave the same at base and head: redirect_slashes through an include, `url_path_for`, the 405 response and `Allow` header, `dependency_overrides`, Starlette `Route` in an included router, and include-level metadata merging in nested includes (prefix, tags, dependencies, response class, unique-id function), which I checked by reading the code.

**Not exercised:** `Host` routes inside included routers, concurrent rebuilds of the candidate cache from threads, and static type-checker or lint deltas.

final:
I found six defects in `refactor/router-tree`. The project's own test suite still passes at head (3181 passed, 13 skipped, 5 xfailed), so none of these are covered by tests.

**What I compared:** head `1e70f7c` against main at the merge-base `016ab76`. The working tree was clean, and I left it that way. I read every changed file: `fastapi/routing.py`, `fastapi/openapi/utils.py`, `fastapi/applications.py`, the docs, the `docs_src` example and the tests. Each probe ran in the given venv, once against a disposable worktree of the base and once against head. The probe scripts and outputs are in `.scratch/router-tree-bugs/` (`probe1.py`/`.out`, `probe2.py`/`.out`).

## Defects

1. **Including a router with no prefix fails if one of its nested routers has a route with an empty path** — `fastapi/routing.py:2438`
   - **Trigger:** this common layout:
     ```python
     items = APIRouter()
     @items.get("")
     ...
     api = APIRouter()
     api.include_router(items, prefix="/items")
     app.include_router(api)
     ```
   - **Consequence:** the empty-path check now looks at the original nested routes, which don't carry their include prefix. `app.include_router(api)` raises `FastAPIError: Prefix and path cannot be both empty (path operation: list_items)` even though the real path is `/items`. The app fails at import.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe1 case A). Base: `GET /items` returns 200. Head: the exception above.
   - **Impact:** apps using this nested-router layout won't start after upgrading.

2. **`request.scope["route"]` no longer has the prefix, tags or dependencies added by the include** — `fastapi/routing.py:1593`
   - **Trigger:** any route from an included router. `_handle_selected` sets `scope["route"]` to the original `APIRoute`, not the combined one.
   - **Consequence:** with `include_router(r, prefix="/v1", tags=["t"])`:
     - Base gives `path='/v1/items/{item_id}'`, `tags=['t']`.
     - Head gives `path='/items/{item_id}'`, `tags=[]`.
   - Metrics and tracing middleware that label requests by `scope["route"].path` would merge routes from different prefixes, or from the same router included twice, under one label. The release notes cover the `router.routes` break but not this one.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe1 case B).
   - **Impact:** observability data is silently wrong. You decide whether the scope should carry the combined route context instead.

3. **`app.openapi()` now overwrites a schema assigned to `app.openapi_schema`** — `fastapi/applications.py:1083`
   - **Trigger:** setting `app.openapi_schema = {...}` without also overriding `app.openapi`.
   - **Consequence:** `_openapi_routes_version` starts as `None`, so the first call regenerates the schema and replaces the custom one. Base keeps the user's schema (title `custom`); head returns the generated one (title `FastAPI`).
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe1 case C).
   - **Impact:** custom or pre-built schemas are lost on `/openapi.json` with no error.

4. **Callbacks from a callback router that includes another router disappear from OpenAPI** — `fastapi/openapi/utils.py:326`
   - **Trigger:** `callbacks=cb.routes`, where `cb` includes another router.
   - **Consequence:** `cb.routes` now holds an internal included-router object, not `APIRoute`s, and `get_openapi_path` skips anything that isn't an `APIRoute`. The operation's `callbacks` comes out as `{}`. Base documents `event_cb`.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe1 case D).
   - **Impact:** the published API docs silently lose their callbacks. The callbacks doc page tells users to pass `.routes`.

5. **`generate_unique_id_function` receives an internal object instead of the `APIRoute`** — `fastapi/routing.py:985`
   - **Trigger:** a custom `generate_unique_id_function` combined with an included router.
   - **Consequence:** for included routes the function is called with the internal `_EffectiveRouteContext`. That object doesn't have the custom route class's attributes and fails `isinstance(route, APIRoute)`.
     - Base produces operationId `R-custom-a`.
     - Head produces `_EffectiveRouteContext-None-a`.
     - A function that reads such an attribute directly would raise `AttributeError`.
   - The changed docs still say the function "receives each `APIRoute`".
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe1 case E).
   - **Impact:** operationIds change, so generated client code and SDK method names change.

6. **Each request to an included route rebuilds its handler, and matching repeats at every include level** — `fastapi/routing.py:1165-1183`, `:1431`, `:1949`
   - **Trigger:** any request served through an included router, which covers most routes in a typical app.
   - **Consequence:**
     - `APIRoute.handle` calls `request_response(self.get_route_handler())` on every request: 2000 `get_request_handler` calls for 2000 requests, versus 0 on base.
     - Each `_match` call walks the router tree again in `_get_routes_version`.
     - `_IncludedRouter.matches` matches the request, then `_handle_selected` matches it again, once per nesting level.
   - In-process timing with 50 routes per level:

     | Include depth | Base | Head |
     |---|---|---|
     | 1 | 63 µs/request | 125 µs/request |
     | 4 | 103 µs/request | 473 µs/request |

   - This also contradicts the new docs line "designed to … avoid adding overhead to each request".
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (probe2).
   - **Impact:** routing overhead goes up for every app that uses `include_router`. These are in-process numbers without a real server, so the share of total latency in a real deployment wasn't measured.

## Minor observations

- **Mounts added after the first request:** a `router.mount(...)` on an already-included router after the first request doesn't take effect (404). Starlette's `mount` and `host` don't increase the router's change counter, so the cached route list isn't refreshed. Base never forwarded mounts at all, and the docs only promise that later path operations show up. It matters only if code mounts things at runtime.
- **Empty-path check skipped for later routes:** that check runs only at include time, so a route with path `""` added to an unprefixed router afterwards is no longer rejected.

## Questions for the author

- For defect 2: should `scope["route"]` expose the combined path and metadata, for example by giving the effective context the same interface as `APIRoute`? Or is the change intended and only missing from the "Breaking Changes" section?

**Not covered:**
- Host routes inside a prefixed include, and sub-apps mounted inside included routers.
- Lifespan handling.

Each defect below was reproduced on head and checked against the same script run on base. **Setup:** The `/tmp` filesystem is out of inodes, so a full base worktree could not be created. ## Defects

1. **`scope["route"]` is now the original route object, without the settings added when its router was included.** `fastapi/routing.py:1593` sets it, and `APIRoute.matches` at `routing.py:1162` does the same.
   - **Trigger:** any route reached through `include_router(..., prefix="/v1")`, read by middleware or an endpoint through `request.scope["route"]`.
   - **Consequence:** `.path` and `.path_format` lose the include prefix. Base returns `/v1/items/{item_id}`; head returns `/items/{item_id}`. The same applies to the route's tags, dependencies, dependant and responses: they no longer include what `include_router(...)` added. Metrics and tracing code that labels requests by route template will report wrong paths, and will merge a router included at `/v1` and `/v2` into one label.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed, `probe1.py`. Middleware also saw `'/items/{item_id}'` on head.
   - **Impact:** the release notes describe `router.routes` as a breaking change but say nothing about `scope["route"]`, so consumers get no warning.

2. **A schema assigned to `app.openapi_schema` is replaced by a generated one.** This is in `fastapi/applications.py:1083`.
   - **Trigger:** assigning `app.openapi_schema = {...}` (for example, one loaded from a file) before the first `app.openapi()` call. `_openapi_routes_version` starts as `None`, so the cache check always fails the first time.
   - **Consequence:** base returns the assigned schema (title `custom`); head generates a fresh one (title `FastAPI`). A related case: if you edit the cached schema in place (for example, adding `x-logo`) and then add a route, the edit is lost when the schema regenerates. Base kept the edit but did not show the new route.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed, `probe1.py`.

3. **Callbacks from a router that includes another router disappear from OpenAPI.** This is in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py:325`.
   - **Trigger:** passing `callbacks=callback_router.routes` (the documented pattern) when `callback_router` contains an `include_router(...)`.
   - **Consequence:** the callback loop only accepts `isinstance(callback, routing.APIRoute)`, so the new included-router entries are skipped. Base emits the `on_event` callback; head emits `"callbacks": {}`. The callback models are still collected through `get_fields_from_routes`, so they appear in components without the operation that uses them.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed, `probe3.py`.

4. **Routing to included routes costs 2–3× more per request, and the updated docs say there is no per-request overhead.**
   - **Where:** `APIRoute.handle` at `routing.py:1167` and the `_IncludedRouter` matching code.
   - **Cause:**
     - Every request to an included route rebuilds `request_response(self.get_route_handler())`.
     - `_IncludedRouter.matches` throws away the match result, so `_handle_selected` matches again, once per nesting level.
     - `effective_candidates()` walks the router subtree (`_get_routes_version`) on every match.
   - **Measurement:** 50 routers × 20 routes, request to the last route, in µs per request:

     | Nesting depth | base | head |
     |---|---|---|
     | 0 | 283 | 657 |
     | 3 | 277 | 865 |

     With a single route, the times are about equal (45 vs 50).
   - **Docs:** `bigger-applications.md` now says inclusion is designed "to avoid adding overhead to each request", which these numbers contradict.
   - **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed, `probe2.py`. Whether this matters depends on the deployment's route count and request rate.

## Minor observations

- **`self.app` replacement is ignored for included routes:** an `APIRoute` subclass that replaces `self.app` in `__init__` works on base but not on head (it returned `"plain"` instead of `"wrapped"`), because `handle` builds a new handler. A subclass that overrides `get_route_handler` without calling `super()` (reading `self.dependant` directly) would likewise skip dependencies added by `include_router`. I inferred that second case from the code and did not run it. Both matter only for undocumented subclassing patterns.
- **Changes after the first request are missed:** `router.mount(...)` and direct `router.routes.append(...)` don't update the routes version, so if they happen after the first request is routed, the cached included routes don't pick them up. Base never included those entries at all, so this is not a regression.

## Checked and fine

These match base or are improvements:
- `dependency_overrides` through an include.
- Trailing-slash redirect and 405 responses (`probe4.py`).
- `url_for`.
- The order in which route, router and include settings take precedence: dependencies, `response_class`, `strict_content_type` and `generate_unique_id_function` match the old code.
- Plain Starlette `Route` entries now get the parent router's prefix, which base dropped. That is a fix.

final:
I found five defects in `refactor/router-tree`. Four are confirmed by running the same probe against both revisions; the fifth comes from reading the code. The most serious ones change what existing users observe: route paths lose their prefix, custom route classes lose their setup, and every request through an included router got slower.

**Scope:** head `1e70f7c` compared with merge-base `016ab76` (which is `main`). Your checkout was clean and was not modified. I exported the `fastapi/` package from each revision into `.scratch/router-tree/{base,head}` and ran the probes there with the venv you gave me. Probe scripts and their output are in that directory too.

## Defects

**1. `request.scope["route"]` no longer carries the full prefixed path** — `fastapi/routing.py:1593` (`_handle_selected`) and `:1162` (`APIRoute.matches`)
- **Trigger:** any route in a router included with a prefix, read through `scope["route"].path` or `.path_format`.
- **Consequence:** `scope["route"]` is now the original `APIRoute`, whose path doesn't include the prefixes. Metrics labels, tracing span names and logging middleware that use this path will report `/items/{item_id}` instead of `/api/items/{item_id}`, so routes that differ only by prefix (`/v1` and `/v2` of the same router) get the same name. The release notes don't mention this break. Plain Starlette `Route`s in the same position still get the prefixed copy, so the behaviour is inconsistent.
- **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`probe1.py`, "scope route path"):
  - base: `{'path': '/api/items/{item_id}', ...}`
  - head: `{'path': '/items/{item_id}', ...}`
- **Action:** you decide. `tests/test_router_include_context.py:351` reads the prefixed path from `scope["fastapi"]["effective_route_context"]`, so this may be intended. If so, it belongs under "Breaking Changes".

**2. Custom `APIRoute` subclasses lose changes made in `__init__`** — `fastapi/routing.py:937-989` (`_EffectiveRouteContext.from_api_route`)
- **Trigger:** a `route_class` that adjusts computed state after `super().__init__()`, for example adding a dependency to `self.dependant`, on a router passed to `include_router`.
- **Consequence:** `main` rebuilt included routes with `type(route)(...)`, so the subclass's `__init__` ran again. The branch rebuilds the state through `_populate_api_route_state` without calling the subclass, so those changes disappear from request handling and OpenAPI. The rewritten `bigger-applications.md` says custom `APIRoute` subclasses "can still participate", which this contradicts.
- **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`probe2.py`, `AuditRoute`):
  - base: `audit dependency ran for: ['/p/audited']`
  - head: `audit dependency ran for: []`

**3. More work on every request through an included router** — `fastapi/routing.py:771-789`, `:1037-1040`, `:1164-1185`
- **Triggers** (all apply to every request):
  - `APIRoute.handle` calls `request_response(self.get_route_handler())` each time, so the request handler is rebuilt per request.
  - `effective_candidates()` walks the whole subtree on each call to work out its change counter.
  - `_match` runs twice: once from `matches()` and again from `_handle_selected()`.
- **Consequence:** a router-heavy app (most FastAPI apps) handles every request more slowly. A custom `get_route_handler` that does setup work or has side effects now runs on every request instead of once. The updated docs promise the opposite ("avoid adding overhead to each request").
- **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`probe2.py`, `probe2_small.py`; ASGI calls with no HTTP client, best of 3 × 500):

| Measurement | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| `get_route_handler` calls in 5 requests | 0 | 5 |
| µs per request, last of 5 included routes | 57 | 78 |
| µs per request, last of 300 included routes | 129 | 390 |

**4. A schema assigned to `app.openapi_schema` is silently overwritten** — `fastapi/applications.py:1083-1084`
- **Trigger:** setting `app.openapi_schema = {...}` before the first call to `app.openapi()`, without overriding `app.openapi`.
- **Consequence:** `_openapi_routes_version` starts as `None`, so the first call regenerates the schema and throws the assigned one away. On `main` it was served. The same check also regenerates the schema after any route is added, discarding in-place edits made to the dict returned earlier.
- **Origin:** new. **Evidence:** executed (`probe1.py`, "user-set openapi_schema"):
  - base: `title: custom`
  - head: `title: FastAPI`
- The documented `custom_openapi` pattern replaces `app.openapi` and is not affected.

**5. Mounts added later are missed by included routers** — `fastapi/routing.py:1037-1056` and `:1947`
- **Trigger:** calling `router.mount(...)` or `router.host(...)` on a router after it has been included and has served a request.
- **Cause:** the cached route list is only refreshed when a change counter goes up. `add_api_route`, `add_route`, `add_websocket_route` and `include_router` increase it; Starlette's `mount`/`host` don't, so the cache keeps serving the old list.
- **Consequence:** the mount answers 404. This contradicts the release note that routes added after inclusion now work. On `main`, mounts inside included routers were never forwarded at all, so this isn't a regression for existing apps.
- **Origin:** new code path. **Evidence:** partly executed. `probe1.py` gives `mounted after: 404` on both revisions. I did not run a mount-before-first-request control on head, so the claim that the stale cache is the cause is from reading the code.

## Outside the change
- **Streaming routes in included routers lose their item schema.** With a JSONL streaming endpoint (`async def ... -> AsyncIterable[Item]`), OpenAPI gives `{'itemSchema': {}}` instead of a `$ref` to `Item`. Directly registered routes get the `$ref`. Both revisions behave the same (`probe1.py`). The cause is that `response_model=None` is passed explicitly, which skips the step that infers the stream item type. The branch rebuilt this exact code path and kept the defect.

## Questions for the author
- Is the change in `scope["route"]` (#1) intended? If so, what should observability integrations read instead?
- Are customisations made in a route class's `__init__` (#2) supposed to keep working under "custom APIRoute subclasses can still participate"?

## Gaps
- `/tmp` was out of inodes, so I couldn't create full worktrees or run the project's test suite. Every result above comes from the targeted probes.
- Not probed: thread safety of the cache rebuild (it runs synchronously with no `await`, so I saw no issue on the event loop), included `Host` routes, websocket dependency overrides through nested includes, and changes to route attributes made after the first request.
- I checked the inheritance of tags, dependencies, responses, callbacks, response class, `generate_unique_id_function`, `strict_content_type`, `deprecated` and `include_in_schema` through nested includes by reading the code. It matches `main`.
